correctness.rationale: Every real unit Birkhoff--James orthogonal pair in \(\ell_4^2\) is parameterized explicitly. The expansion of \(\|x+\lambda y\|_4^4\) reduces to \(A,B\) with the exact identity \(B^2=A(1-A^2)\). Boundary analysis forces any value below one for the normalized denominator to an interior critical point; the stationary system has one feasible root \(A^2=(5-\sqrt{17})/12\), at which \(F=(5-\sqrt{17})/2\). Thus the reciprocal fourth power is \((5+\sqrt{17})/4\). The packaged checker separately verifies the algebraic critical equations and value at high precision; finite computation is not used as the proof of the global minimum.

value.rationale: The same-invariant primary literature explicitly identifies exact generalized rectangular constants as generally unknown and develops bounds for canonical \(\ell_p\) spaces. The exponent-four, two-dimensional case is a natural benchmark: it is the first non-Hilbert even exponent where the Birkhoff--James equation and fourth-power norm expansion close algebraically. The exact value is nontrivial, is not implied by the published upper estimate, and provides a sharp reference point for future work on \(\mu_p(\ell_p)\) and for testing general inequalities.
